# IDENTIFYING CONGRUENCE SUBGROUPS OF THE MODULAR GROUP

TIM HSU

(Communicated by Ronald M. Solomon)

**Abstract.** We exhibit a simple test (Theorem 2.4) for determining if a given (classical) modular subgroup is a congruence subgroup, and give a detailed description of its implementation (Theorem 3.1). In an appendix, we also describe a more “invariant” and arithmetic congruence test.

## 1. NOTATION

We describe (conjugacy classes of) subgroups Γ ⊂ PSL₂(Z) in terms of permutation representations of PSL₂(Z), following Millington [11, 12] and Atkin and Swinnerton-Dyer [1].

We recall that a conjugacy class of subgroups of PSL₂(Z) is equivalent to a transitive permutation representation of PSL₂(Z). Such a representation can be defined by transitive permutations E and V which satisfy the relations

(1.1)  1 = E² = V³.

The relations (1.1) are fulfilled by

(1.2)  E = \(\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}\),  V = \(\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}\).

Alternately, such a representation can be defined by transitive permutations L and R which satisfy

(1.3)  1 = (LR⁻¹L)² = (R⁻¹L)³,

with the relations being fulfilled by

(1.4)  L = \(\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\),  R = \(\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\).

One can also use permutations E and L such that

(1.5)  1 = E² = (L⁻¹E)³,

with E and L corresponding to the indicated matrices in (1.2) and (1.4), respectively.

The Conjugacy Problem of The Modular Group and The Class Number of Real Quadratic Number Fields

This document discusses the conjugacy problem of the modular group and its application to computing the class number of certain real quadratic number fields. The author, Charles Traina, presents theorems related to the modular group and its trace polynomials, utilizing Olga Taussky's theorem to derive results about ideal classes in these number fields. The paper aims to provide a framework for understanding the relationship between the structure of the modular group and the properties of real quadratic fields.

We propose to reverse the case of the theorem which had been men-
tioned [ 19481 by Olga Taussky in a letter to Wilhelm Magnus. She obser-
ved that all elements of order two (i.e., with trace zero) are conjugate in
PSL(2,Z) and, similarly, all elements of order three with trace + 1, since
the corresponding quadratic fields have class number one. Exercise 4,
p. 133 in Magnus [2] is based on this remark which can also be derived
most easily from the Kurosh subgroup theorem according to which the
elements of finite order in a free product are conjugates of elements of tinite
order in the factors, PSL(2,Z) being the free product of a group of order 3
and a group of order 2. (Since, in the upper complex half plane z = i is a
fixed point of an element of order 2 in PSL(2, Z), the images of z = i under
the action of this group must be exactly the fixed points of the other
elements of order 2 which are of the form (a + i)/c, where a, c are integers,
c > 0, and c divides a2 + 1.) In our paper, we shall again use the abstract
theory of PSL(2,Z) to derive results about numbers of ideal classes in real
quadratic number fields.
